reason: I'll start with the worn red cells: the picture shows recycling cells breaking them down, which should help recover their iron.
expectation: I expect the recycling cells to release iron that the marrow can reuse, though there may be another step before new red cells form.

alternatives.reason: Growing replacement skin cells also matches a goal, but I want to follow the iron-recycling route first.

effect: The recovered iron is carried in blood, so I can follow it to the marrow to make new red cells.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the iron reused rather than discarded.
reason: The marrow contains developing blood cells and nutrients, making it the natural next step in the iron-recycling goal.
expectation: I expect the marrow to use the recovered iron in new red blood cells.

alternatives.reason: Skin replacement is also a goal, but I want to finish following the iron first.

effect: The recovered iron became part of haemoglobin in new red cells, completing that goal. Skin replacement remains.
reaction: Seeing the iron reused in new cells makes the recycling route clear.
reason: This is the only available combination, and it supplies the dividing skin cells with materials for growth.
expectation: I expect the cells to grow and produce replacement skin cells while some remain at the base.

effect: The new skin cells form beneath the surface while the base cells remain and older cells shed, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The picture makes continuous skin replacement easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following recovered iron into new red blood cells was most worthwhile: it showed what gets reused and where it ends up.

leastWorthwhile.text: The skin-cell combination was the least engaging decision because it was the only action left, although its result was clear.

surprise.text: The recovered iron travels in blood attached to proteins before becoming part of the oxygen-carrying protein in new red cells.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals gave both combinations a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would probably continue if another chapter offered a similarly clear connection, though this short chapter had few meaningful choices.
